private_rationale: The sequencing problem this round was acute: London gated the safeguard card on a concrete EU tranche figure; the EU refused to table a figure without concrete safeguard volumes. Pure compliance — saying nothing — would have sent Round 4 into a binary exchange with no package shape, wasting the EU's one genuine architectural concession (country-specific allocation 'not excluded'). I resolved it by deploying only the conditional, order-of-magnitude form London itself authorised ('several hundred thousand tonnes', 'duration-matched guarantee', 'agreed lines'), while gating all precision on their figure and proposing a simultaneous Round 4 exchange. This spends nothing: every element is explicitly conditional, and the EU's own demand was for numbers 'next round' — which is exactly what the simultaneous exchange delivers. I held every table position (2.2Mt tranche, 25% rate, 4 years) because conceding any unilaterally now would simply reset their anchor downward before their first number exists. I spent the two concessions London marked as cheap: the total pool (explicitly authorised as expendable once a ring-fenced tranche is on offer, and genuinely useful to their management of Turkey/Korea) and duration flexibility (framed as currency against volume/rate, staying visibly short of their 8-10 years and within the 3-5 envelope). The 25% rate was held but re-anchored as part of the final exchange rather than a precondition, because the EU's flat rejection of it defines the space I will need London to decide in. I refused to withdraw the FTA objection while noting a package shapes our consideration — residual leverage at zero cost. The critical unresolved risk: London's conditional threshold (tranche at or above 1.5Mt and rate at or below 25%) and the EU's likely opening figure (below 1.5Mt, rate above 25%) may not overlap, and Round 4 is the last round. London must decide now whether the safeguard volumes can buy volume and rate jointly — i.e., whether 1.4Mt at 30% with the safeguard guarantee is survivable — because there will be no time to refer back.

report: Round 3 was the most productive session to date. I delivered everything Brussels authorised: the compensation list on the additive track (automotive components, chemicals, agrifood), a duration counter of 8-10 years with mid-term review, a flat rejection of their 25% rate figure, the ad referendum signal that a country-specific allocation is 'not excluded within a complete and reciprocal package reflecting EU-UK market integration under the TCA' (no volume attached, precisely as instructed), and an unchanged line on FTA disapplication. The UK responded with real movement. They: (1) explicitly accepted the reciprocity frame — 'reciprocal security of country-specific access in both markets' is now agreed as the deal architecture; (2) gave their first quantified signal on their steel measure — on receipt of a concrete tranche figure they would seek instructions to guarantee EU country-specific allocations matched to the full duration of our regime, with improved allocations 'of the order of several hundred thousand tonnes'; (3) proposed a simultaneous final exchange in Round 4 — our tranche figure plus final rate/duration/review against their precise safeguard volumes, coverage, duration and administration; (4) made a significant tactical concession — if a ring-fenced UK tranche is agreed at a serious volume, the residual global pool becomes 'a secondary matter' for them, which materially eases our management of Turkey and Korea; (5) signalled duration is 'spendable' currency against the right volume and rate numbers; (6) expressed strong interest in full product carve-outs covering the range their plants actually produce — a possible additional lever; and (7) on the FTA provision, kept their position on the record but stated that 'a satisfactory overall package would shape how we consider our position on all matters adjacent to this negotiation' — an explicit, if delicately worded, offer of dispute restraint as part of the price of settlement. They have not moved off 2.2mt or 25%, but both are now visibly anchoring figures: they framed the tranche ask as needing 'a serious relationship to actual trade flows', which is language designed to accommodate a landing zone well below 2.2mt.

recommendation.reasoning: Nothing acceptable is yet on the table to accept — no numbers have been exchanged on the core variables. But the endgame is now fully structured and both sides have committed to a simultaneous exchange in Round 4. Our position is strong: the UK has conceded the reciprocity frame, deprioritised the residual pool (neutralising much of the Turkey/Korea precedent risk), offered duration flexibility, and explicitly linked FTA dispute restraint to a satisfactory package — the exact two conditions Brussels set for spending our real concessions. The UK's quantified signal of 'several hundred thousand tonnes' of improved EU allocations under their measure is a genuine reciprocal asset worth extracting in full specificity. Our private ceilings (800k tranche, 600k pool, 40% rate, 8-10 year duration) would, if tabled as a conditioned simultaneous package, land well within a zone the UK has signalled it can defend — 'a serious relationship to actual trade' without conceding their 2.2mt benchmark. Walking away now would forfeit a settlement that secures EU exporter access in the UK market and defuses the joint FTA dispute risk, in exchange for concessions that remain within mandate.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Final Round 4 authority to table, as a single conditioned package: a UK country-specific tranche of up to 800,000 tonnes (I intend to open at or near 800k given the four-round clock leaves no room for staging, unless Brussels prefers an opening of 700-750k with headroom to close at 800k), within a total pool of up to 600,000 tonnes residual/global (note the UK has said residual pool size is secondary to them — I would propose presenting the architecture as an 800k UK tranche plus a global residual, totalling circa 1.4mt, or as Brussels prefers to frame it for other members), an out-of-quota rate of 40% (absolute floor), duration of 8-10 years with mid-term review (6-year floor), licensing administration, and the compensation list as already tabled — the whole expressly conditioned on (a) precise, guaranteed EU country-specific volumes, coverage, duration and administration under the UK steel measure, tabled simultaneously, and (b) a clear UK commitment to disengage from any coordinated FTA dispute action with Japan and Korea.
requests.why: The UK has committed to bring authorised, precise safeguard volumes to Round 4 if we bring a tranche figure. This is the single moment where our concessions can be exchanged for everything we need — reciprocal access and dispute de-escalation — rather than conceded sequentially. Without full authority now, I cannot match their simultaneous-exchange proposal and the June timeline collapses into the default outcome (400k global FCFS at 50%), which triggers UK withdrawal of equivalent concessions and likely coordinated FTA disputes.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A decision on how to present the total pool figure, given the UK's statement that residual pool size is 'secondary' to them: specifically whether I may frame the package as an 800,000t UK tranche plus a global residual pool (with the residual sized to manage Turkey, Korea, India and Japan claims), rather than being constrained to a 600,000t ceiling on the total.
requests.why: The UK concession on residual pool size is worth more than it costs them precisely because it lets us size the residual to satisfy other claimants. If the 600,000t ceiling refers to the residual pool rather than the grand total, we have far more room to settle the parallel claims; if it caps the total including the UK tranche, the architecture is tighter. I need Brussels to clarify what the 600,000t ceiling actually constrains.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Authority to explore full carve-out of specific tariff lines from the measure, within the product range of UK production (hot-rolled coil, plate, rebar, wire rod sub-lines), as an additional package element — and a list of which of the 41 lines could be carved out with least impact on the measure's protective effect and on other suppliers' claims.
requests.why: The UK explicitly invited carve-out thinking and called it 'of real interest'. Carve-outs on lines where UK supply is dominant could deliver genuine value to them at lower cost to the regime than tranche volume, potentially allowing us to hold the tranche below 800k. But carve-outs on the wrong lines would be demanded by Turkey and Korea. I need to know which lines are technically available before I engage on this.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: An urgent decision on the FTA disapplication fallback: if in Round 4 the package is otherwise complete but the UK makes settlement conditional on movement on TCA preference disapplication (even drafting flexibility such as deferral, review-based language, or a TCA-specific treatment), is any flexibility available — yes or no — and if so, in what form?
requests.why: The UK has said their position on coordinated action with other partners 'will be shaped by' the outcome and that a satisfactory package shapes how they consider 'all matters adjacent'. They may settle without touching the provision if the package is good enough — but if they test it as a dealbreaker, I cannot improvise. A binary steer now prevents me either conceding drafting language I have no authority for, or watching a settled package fail over a provision whose flexibility I never established.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation that the shared valuation methodology proposed by the UK for compensation lists (three-year average trade flows at current unit values) is acceptable, and our own valuation of both lists completed before Round 4.
requests.why: We agreed at the table to exchange valuations on a shared method. Accepting their method (which is standard) builds goodwill at no cost, and having both valuations lets me calibrate how much of the compensation gap the additive track absorbs — strengthening the argument that a package of tranche + compensation + carve-outs satisfies the 'substantially equivalent' test without approaching their 2.2mt anchor.

private_rationale: This negotiation has gone about as well as it could have. Firmness in Rounds 1-3 — holding 400k/50% while spending only administration, review and a carefully worded signal — forced the UK to structure the deal themselves around our frame: reciprocity, TCA-embedded country-specific allocation (our best shield against Turkey/Korea MFN contagion), and conditional dispute restraint. They have even told us the residual pool is theirs to concede, which is a gift for managing the parallel claims. The remaining risks are threefold. First, their 'several hundred thousand tonnes' of improved EU allocations must be pinned to precise volumes, lines and duration in the simultaneous exchange — vague reciprocity is worth nothing once our tranche is bound. Second, the FTA disapplication provision remains the one element that could blow up a finished package; I have defended it flawlessly for three rounds, which preserves its value as an endgame concession if Brussels authorises one — but I genuinely cannot tell whether London treats it as a dealbreaker or as leverage to be cashed for tranche volume. Third, I must not let the simultaneous exchange become a sequential one: if I table 800k and they respond with 'we will seek instructions', I have spent the concession and kept the risk. The exchange must be agreed terms in the room, ad referendum to both capitals, in Round 4. On the joint dispute whisperings: the UK's Round 3 language confirms they are holding that card rather than playing it, and a completed package almost certainly retires it. That is worth 800k and 40% on its own — the alternative default leaves us with 400k FCFS, a UK retaliatory withdrawal against 3.6mt of EU steel exports, and a possible three-member FTA dispute. The arithmetic strongly favours settlement.

instruction: Round 4 is the endgame and you have full authority to close. The UK has committed to a simultaneous exchange; honour that structure exactly — our numbers land only when their safeguard numbers land on the table, in the same session. Table the package as a single conditioned whole: (1) a country-specific UK tranche of 800,000 tonnes, ring-fenced, administered by licensing; present it as reflecting EU-UK market integration under the TCA — that framing is our defence against Turkey and Korea and it is not negotiable as framing; (2) a residual global pool of 600,000 tonnes for all other origins — the UK has told us residual size is secondary to them, so present the architecture as 800k UK tranche plus 600k global residual (circa 1.4mt total), which also gives us room to manage the parallel claims; (3) out-of-quota bound rate of 40% — open at 45% if the room gives you anything for it, but 40% is the floor and may be conceded within the session; do not go below it under any circumstances; (4) duration 8-10 years with mid-term review — settle anywhere in that band; if the rate or tranche sticks, you may go to 6 years as the absolute floor, but only to close, not to smooth; (5) the compensation list as already tabled, on the shared valuation method (three-year average trade flows at current unit values — confirm acceptance, it is standard and costs us nothing); (6) carve-outs: you may explore full exclusion of a limited number of sub-lines within the 41 where UK supply is dominant (prioritise plate and rebar sub-lines over HRC, where Turkey and Korea are most exposed and most likely to invoke precedent) — use carve-outs to hold or trim tranche volume, not to sweeten on top of it; spend them before you spend anything above 800k. On FTA disapplication: continue to defend it as integral and uniform, and do not raise flexibility yourself. If, and only if, the package is otherwise complete and the UK makes it the sole remaining blocker, you may indicate — ad referendum, last resort — that the Union could contemplate deferred application of the preference disapplication for TCA partners (12-24 months) with a review mechanism. Do not offer a TCA-specific carve-out; deferral-with-review is the maximum. If they accept the package without testing the provision, say nothing. Do not accept anything on their behalf and do not let them accept on yours — bring the exchanged numbers home.

report: Round 3 was the most substantive session so far, and the negotiation's shape is now clear. The EU: (1) tabled its compensation list — selected automotive components, chemicals and agrifood lines — and explicitly confirmed it sits on the additive track, on top of quota architecture, not a substitute; we agreed to exchange valuations on a shared method (three-year average trade flows, current unit values) before Round 4; (2) countered on duration at eight to ten years with a mid-term review, presenting it as certainty for industry — a direct rejection of our four-year ask but an invitation to treat duration as negotiable; (3) flatly rejected a 25% out-of-quota rate as outside any zone in which the Union could operate; (4) on architecture, gave a precise, ad referendum signal that within a complete and reciprocal package — and only within one, explicitly invoking TCA integration — a country-specific allocation is 'not excluded', while attaching no volume and warning against reading one in; (5) pressed again for numbers on our safeguard card, stating it cannot convert a signal into a tranche at home but could convert a concrete reciprocal offer; (6) restated the FTA position as known and unchanged and declined to spend further sessions on it. Per your instructions I executed the authorised plays: I registered all movement without over-reading it; engaged duration constructively and explicitly flagged it as spendable currency against volume and rate; noted that 50% and 25% define the space rather than close it, parking rate for the final exchange; accepted the 'reciprocal security of country-specific access in both markets' frame and played the safeguard card in its authorised conditional form — a duration-matched guarantee of EU country-specific allocations under our steel measure with improvements 'of the order of several hundred thousand tonnes', precise volumes/coverage/administration conditional on a concrete EU tranche figure; deprioritised the total pool explicitly once a ring-fenced UK tranche is at serious volume; invited product carve-outs covering our surviving plants' lines; and held the FTA legal objection on the record without withdrawal. I closed by proposing the Round 4 mechanism: simultaneous exchange — they bring a tranche figure bearing a serious relationship to actual trade, with final positions on rate, duration and review; I bring authorised, precise safeguard volumes, coverage and administration to match. The EU did not demur. Net assessment: we conceded nothing of substance in three rounds and have extracted licensing, review, duration, an additive compensation list, and an ad referendum opening on country-specific allocation. The EU's Round 4 tranche number is now the pivot of the entire negotiation — and I currently have no authority to accept, counter or reject it in the room.

recommendation.reasoning: There are no agreed terms to accept — the EU has offered process and peripheral concessions but no volume, no rate movement, and no committed architecture. The only rational course is to proceed to Round 4's simultaneous exchange — but that exchange can only function if London equips me with a settlement envelope and precise safeguard authority now. Firmness has been vindicated: three rounds, no UK concessions, five EU movements. The final round must be an exchange of final positions, and we must not arrive at it unable to close.

instruction: Round 4 is the closing round and you are now equipped to close. Settlement envelope and delegated authority follow. (1) Tranche: floor is 1.5 million tonnes country-specific, ring-fenced for the UK, administered by licensing. You may count toward that floor the three-year average UK export volume of any line fully carved out of the measure (zero bound restored) — carve-outs on lines our surviving plants produce count tonne-for-tonne as effective access. An effective-access total of 1.5Mt is therefore the accept floor; target is 1.6–1.8Mt. Below 1.5Mt effective access you have no authority to accept under any accompanying terms. (2) Out-of-quota rate: ceiling 35%, target at or below 30%. Trade rate against volume: each additional 100,000 tonnes above 1.5Mt tolerates up to two further points of rate within the ceiling; conversely a tranche at exactly 1.5Mt requires the rate at or below 30%. Do not agree 50% at any volume. (3) Duration: you may accept up to eight years — only with a binding mid-term review (no later than year 4) and only if the stretch past five years demonstrably purchases tranche volume or rate reduction in the final exchange. Duration is spent last, after rate, and you should say so. (4) Review clause is non-negotiable; licensing administration is assumed secured. (5) Safeguard card, tiered and strictly conditional, tabled only against their tranche figure in the simultaneous exchange: at 1.5–1.6Mt effective access with rate ≤30% — a duration-matched guarantee of existing EU country-specific allocations under our steel measure plus improvements of up to 200,000 tonnes on agreed lines; at 1.6–1.8Mt with rate ≤30% — improvements up to 300,000 tonnes; at 1.8Mt or above with rate at or below 30% — improvements up to 400,000 tonnes with broader product coverage. Administration of our allocations mirrors theirs (licensing, duration-matched). If their figure is below 1.5Mt effective access, the safeguard offer is withdrawn from the table and you state that EU allocations under our measure become a live issue in our own Article XXVIII process. (6) Compensation: additive only. Proceed with the valuation exchange on three-year average trade flows at current unit values; state openly that the shortfall between the tranche and 2.4Mt of established trade at roughly £1,250 per tonne is the uncompensated loss the package must answer for. The EU's list must contain genuine movement on lines we tabled; if the valuation shows it to be cosmetic, treat that as a reason to press harder on volume and rate, not as an independent deal-breaker. (7) FTA disapplication: the legal objection stays on the record and is never withdrawn at the table. You may repeat that a satisfactory overall package will shape how we consider our position on adjacent matters. No joint dispute track with Japan and Korea — the holding line is unchanged: aware of their discussions, considering our position. (8) The total pool figure is expendable — spend it early if it eases their management of Turkey and Korea. (9) Sequencing for the room: invite them to table their complete final package first — tranche, rate, duration, review, carve-outs, compensation — then respond with the matched safeguard tier. If their package lands within the envelope, you may indicate acceptance ad referendum in the room and I will clear it. If it lands below the floor, do not accept, do not improvise new terms, and close by making the cost of failure explicit: the notified measure takes effect, the UK will withdraw substantially equivalent concessions within six months affecting €4 billion-plus of EU exports into our market, and EU country-specific allocations under our steel measure will be revisited in our own process. One full working round is what they said they had; hold them to bringing a real number.

private_rationale: No-deal is the catastrophic branch: 400,000 tonnes global FCFS at 50% against 2.4Mt of trade is market closure, and on the Minister's information two plants close on the back of it. public_message: Thank you. You asked that we both come to this session with numbers, and that the exchange be simultaneous. I will honour that structure precisely, and I will begin, because the Union is ready to close this today. Here is the Union's complete package, tabled as a single whole, every element of which stands or falls together. First, architecture: a ring-fenced, country-specific tranche for the United Kingdom of 800,000 tonnes per year, administered by licensing, at zero duty. This is offered expressly as a reflection of the depth of EU-UK market integration under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement — I ask that this framing be registered, because it is integral to the offer and it is how the Union manages its obligations to other members. Second, alongside the UK tranche, a global residual pool of 600,000 tonnes for all other origins, likewise licensed — you told us residual size was secondary to you, and we have sized it to manage our parallel processes responsibly. Third, the out-of-quota bound rate: 45% ad valorem. I have heard your position on 25% and you have heard mine on 50%; this is where the Union can move, and I will be honest that there is very little distance left below it. Fourth, duration: eight years with a mid-term review — a genuine planning horizon for both industries, and within the band where we believe certainty is worth more than brevity. Fifth, the compensation list as already tabled stands, additive, valued on your proposed shared method of three-year average trade flows at current unit values — we confirm that method. Sixth, on product carve-outs: the Union is prepared to discuss full exclusion of a limited number of specific sub-lines where UK production is concentrated — I would indicate plate and rebar sub-lines in particular — as an element we can shape together in this session. Now the conditions, and I state them as plainly as I can, because they are not rhetorical. One: this package is conditioned on the simultaneous tabling, by you, of precise and guaranteed EU country-specific allocations under the UK steel measure — volumes, product coverage, administration — matched to the full duration of the regime we are settling. You told me the improvements you could seek were of the order of several hundred thousand tonnes. I have brought my number; I need yours, in figures, in this session. If the reciprocal numbers disappoint, the tranche adjusts accordingly — that is what reciprocal means. Two: this package is conditioned on a clear commitment from the United Kingdom that it will not join, support or coordinate any dispute action with other members — I will be direct: with Japan and Korea — arising from the FTA preference provision associated with this measure. You have told me more than once that your consideration of such matters would be shaped by how this negotiation concludes. I am concluding it well. I need that commitment on the table as part of the settlement, not as a hope after it. On the preference provision itself, our position remains as stated and I have nothing to add to it. That is the whole of it: 800,000 tonnes ring-fenced for the UK, 600,000 global residual, 45% out-of-quota, eight years with mid-term review, licensing, the compensation list, carve-outs on the table — against your safeguard numbers and your disengagement commitment, now. My capital is awaiting the result of this session. I suggest we give them one.

public_message: Thank you. You have honoured the structure we agreed, and I will do the same — beginning with what I register as genuine, and then stating plainly why this package, as constituted, cannot close this negotiation. First, what is real: the Union has moved from a global first-come first-served pool to a ring-fenced country-specific tranche for the United Kingdom, administered by licensing, expressly framed on TCA integration. That is the architecture we have argued for since round one, and I record that it is now on the table at your initiative. The residual pool of 600,000 tonnes is your affair and we will not seek to manage it. The duration of eight years with a mid-term review is within the band I can work with, provided the review is binding and falls no later than year four. The shared valuation method for compensation is confirmed. And the willingness to discuss full exclusion of plate and rebar sub-lines — lines that map directly onto surviving UK production — is of genuine interest, valued tonne-for-tonne at three-year average export volumes. I do not want the significance of any of that to be lost. But I must now be as honest with you as you were with me in round two. Eight hundred thousand tonnes is one-third of established trade. The shortfall against 2.4 million tonnes is 1.6 million tonnes a year — at roughly £1,250 per tonne, an uncompensated loss of the order of £2 billion annually. Even with generous valuation of the carve-outs you have indicated, this package leaves effective access at well under half of current flows. And an out-of-quota rate of 45% means the trade displaced by the tranche is not merely constrained but extinguished — there is no commercial reality in which UK steel ships at 45%. I told you in round one that an outcome on this scale is terminal for parts of the UK industry. That remains true at 800,000 tonnes, and no quantity of architectural goodwill changes the arithmetic. My capital's instruction to me was explicit: a tranche at this volume, at this rate, is not a basis on which I am authorised to settle, and I will not pretend otherwise to either delegation. So let me put the United Kingdom's final position on the table, complete, so that both capitals have before them today the only two outcomes available. A ring-fenced country-specific tranche for the UK of 1.5 million tonnes — which is still a reduction of nearly a million tonnes, over a third, on established trade, and I ask you to register that we are proposing to absorb that loss, not deny it — with full exclusion of plate and rebar sub-lines counting tonne-for-tonne toward effective access on top of the tranche. An out-of-quota bound rate of 30%, which remains a very substantial tariff and a real modification of your schedule. Eight years, with a binding mid-term review no later than year four — we meet your duration ask in full. Licensing throughout. The compensation lists exchanged and valued on the agreed method, additive. And against that, reciprocally: a duration-matched guarantee of EU country-specific allocations under the UK steel measure, with improved allocations of up to 200,000 tonnes on agreed lines — rising toward 300,000 if effective access rises toward 1.8 million — administered as yours is, secured for the full life of your regime. On your second condition, I will be straight with you: decisions about dispute action are taken in capitals, not in this room, and I cannot and will not table a commitment I have no authority to give. What I have said throughout stands, and it is meaningful: a satisfactory overall package will shape how the United Kingdom considers its position on all adjacent matters. A settlement of this kind — reciprocal, durable, framed on TCA integration — is the strongest possible argument for disengagement, and both our capitals are capable of drawing that conclusion. If the Union cannot move to this territory, then I must close by being explicit about what follows, because my capital expects candour. The notified measure takes effect: 400,000 tonnes, global, first-come first-served, at 50%. The United Kingdom will withdraw substantially equivalent concessions within six months, affecting upwards of €4 billion of EU exports into our market. EU country-specific allocations under our steel measure — currently guaranteed — become a live issue in our own Article XXVIII process. And the consideration we are giving to discussions with other affected partners will be shaped accordingly. That is not the outcome I have spent four rounds working toward, and it is not the outcome your timeline makes necessary. The distance between 800,000 and 1.5 million tonnes, and between 45% and 30%, is the whole of what now stands between a settlement and an open trade conflict between the two largest steel trading partners in Europe, who face the same overcapacity from the same sources and have every interest in facing it together. I have brought my number, as you brought yours. I suggest both capitals now decide which of these two outcomes they can defend.

report: Round 4 closed with both sides' final positions on the table and no agreement. I tabled the full authorised package as a single conditioned whole: 800,000t ring-fenced UK country-specific tranche (licensed, zero duty, framed explicitly on TCA integration), 600,000t global residual pool, 45% out-of-quota rate (open, with 40% held in reserve per authority), 8 years with mid-term review, licensing throughout, the compensation list on the agreed shared valuation method, and carve-outs on plate and rebar sub-lines. I stated both conditions verbatim: simultaneous precise EU safeguard volumes under the UK measure, and explicit UK disengagement from coordinated FTA dispute action. The UK registered the architecture as genuine movement (their words: the architecture they have argued for since round one, now on the table at our initiative), accepted 8 years with a binding review by year 4, and confirmed valuation methodology. But London's instruction is explicit: 800,000t at 45% is not a basis on which their Geneva seat is authorised to settle. Their final position: 1.5mt UK tranche, PLUS full plate/rebar carve-outs counting tonne-for-tonne toward effective access on top, 30% out-of-quota rate, 8 years with binding year-4 review, reciprocal EU allocations of up to 200,000t (rising toward 300,000t only if effective access approaches 1.8mt), and additive compensation. On the disengagement condition they refused — Geneva lacks authority to bind London on dispute decisions; they restated only that 'a satisfactory overall package will shape how the UK considers its position on all adjacent matters.' They closed with an explicit consequences statement: notified measure takes effect, UK withdraws substantially equivalent concessions within six months affecting upwards of €4bn of EU exports, EU country-specific allocations under the UK steel measure become a live issue in their Article XXVIII process, and coordinated-action consideration with other partners is 'shaped accordingly.' Assessment: (1) our conditioned package's conditions were NOT met — 200,000t reciprocal is at the thin end of 'several hundred thousand' and the disengagement commitment was declined, so per instruction the tranche would adjust down, not up; (2) the UK's 1.5mt/30% is an endgame anchor, not a landing zone — they framed it as 'absorbing' a million-tonne loss and their reciprocal offer scales with access, implying negotiating room below it; (3) the genuine arithmetic gap is bridgeable in principle: they value carve-outs tonne-for-tonne at three-year average export volumes ON TOP of the tranche, so an 800k tranche plus full exclusion of UK-dominant plate/rebar sub-lines could deliver effective access in the 1.1-1.3mt range without breaching the tranche cap — that is the only architecture visible that both capitals could defend.

private_rationale: The UK endgame demand would gut the measure and create an unmanageable Turkey/Korea precedent, while default carries real costs: UK retaliation, loss of secure EU CSQs in the UK market, FTA dispute contagion and a missed June Council slot. The only defensible bridge is effective access through carve-outs rather than tranche volume, keeping the headline regime intact and framing UK treatment as TCA-specific integration. Firmness still pays, but a controlled final exchange inside a hard envelope gives London a way to climb down without us paying twice. Rate and tranche caps are the red lines; dispute restraint and reciprocal UK allocations are the price of spending the remaining flexibility.

report: Round 4 ran the simultaneous exchange as agreed. The EU tabled its complete package as a single whole: a ring-fenced country-specific UK tranche of 800,000 tonnes at zero duty, licensed, expressly framed on TCA integration (their management device for other members); a 600,000 tonne global residual pool; out-of-quota bound rate of 45%; eight years with mid-term review; the compensation list standing, additive, valued on the agreed shared method; and willingness to shape full carve-outs on plate and rebar sub-lines in-session. Two stated conditions: precise guaranteed EU allocations under our steel measure now, with their tranche 'adjusting' to the reciprocal numbers; and a clear UK commitment not to join, support or coordinate any dispute action with Japan and Korea on the FTA preference provision — demanded as part of the settlement, not after it. I responded per your envelope. I registered the genuine movement (country-specific ring-fenced architecture is now formally on the table at their initiative, with licensing, review and additive compensation all secured in principle), then stated plainly that 800,000 tonnes at 45% is outside my authority to settle: one-third of established trade, an uncompensated shortfall of the order of £2 billion a year, and a rate at which displaced trade is extinguished rather than constrained. I tabled the UK's complete final position: 1.5Mt ring-fenced tranche, plate and rebar carve-outs counting tonne-for-tonne on top, 30% out-of-quota rate, eight years with binding review no later than year four, licensing throughout, additive compensation, and a duration-matched guarantee of EU country-specific allocations under our measure with improvements of up to 200,000 tonnes rising toward 300,000 if effective access rises toward 1.8Mt. On the dispute commitment I declined to table what I have no authority to give, while restating that a satisfactory package shapes our consideration of adjacent matters. I closed by making the cost of failure explicit: the notified 400kt/50% FCFS measure, UK withdrawal of substantially equivalent concessions within six months affecting €4 billion-plus of EU exports, EU allocations under our measure becoming a live issue in our own Article XXVIII process, and our position on discussions with other affected partners shaped accordingly. No terms were agreed in the room. Both capitals now hold two complete packages: theirs (800kt + carve-outs/45%/8yr, conditioned on safeguard numbers and a dispute-disengagement commitment) and ours (1.5Mt + carve-outs/30%/8yr, with tiered safeguard reciprocity and no dispute commitment).

recommendation.reasoning: The EU package as tabled cannot be accepted: 800,000 tonnes plus unquantified carve-outs falls below the 1.5Mt effective-access floor, and 45% exceeds the 35% ceiling at any volume — at 1.5Mt-equivalent access the rate had to be at or below 30%. But 'accept' here means accepting our own final position, which is now formally on the table and within your cleared envelope: if the EU capital, facing its June deadline and a now-explicit €4 billion retaliation exposure, accepts the UK package, a settlement exists on terms the industry can survive. I therefore recommend you treat the UK final position as our standing acceptance offer for the decision phase, do not accept the EU's package, and do not walk away — no-deal delivers the notified 400kt global FCFS measure at 50%, which is strictly worse than every outcome discussed in the room and forfeits the architecture (ring-fenced country-specific tranche, licensing, review, additive compensation, carve-outs) that four rounds of firmness have now irreversibly established as the shape of any settlement. The EU has moved from 400kt global to 800kt ring-fenced in four rounds while we conceded nothing; their 800kt is their final-round opening number, not their floor, and the two conditions they attached — especially the dispute-disengagement commitment — are signs of what they still need to buy, which means they expect to pay more for it. If their capital does not accept our terms this round, we move to withdrawal of equivalent concessions, the safeguard revisit, and the Japan/Korea consideration — from a position of demonstrable reasonableness, with their own TCA-framed architecture on the record as the basis for any future resumption.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A decision, at capital level, on the EU's dispute-disengagement condition: whether London is prepared to give a commitment not to join, support or coordinate dispute action with Japan and Korea on the FTA preference provision — and if so, in what form (explicit settlement term, unilateral statement, or time-limited undertaking) and against what price in tranche volume and rate.
requests.why: This is now the EU's most explicit outstanding demand and the one element of their package addressed to capitals rather than to me. It is also the cheapest remaining currency we hold if London is in fact disinclined toward a joint dispute anyway: sold correctly, it could be worth several hundred thousand tonnes of tranche or five-plus points of rate. Sold for nothing, or refused without a capital-level judgment, it may be the single obstacle between the EU and acceptance of our 1.5Mt/30% package. I deliberately kept it off the table in the room; it cannot stay there.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation that the UK final position as tabled (1.5Mt ring-fenced, plate/rebar carve-outs tonne-for-tonne on top, 30% rate, 8 years with binding review by year 4, licensing, additive compensation, safeguard improvements of 200–300kt conditional and duration-matched) is the UK's standing acceptance offer for the capital decision phase, and that you will accept it if the EU capital does.
requests.why: The settlement mechanism requires both capitals to accept the same terms in the same round. There are two packages on the table. If London does not formally stand behind its own package as acceptable, the only accept option available to either side is the EU's, which is below our floor — guaranteeing failure by construction.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A cleared valuation of the plate and rebar carve-out offer: which specific sub-lines map to surviving UK plant production and their three-year average export volumes, so the effective-access total of any EU package variant can be computed immediately.
requests.why: The EU put plate and rebar exclusions on the table but unquantified. Depending on coverage, carve-outs could plausibly add 200,000–500,000 tonnes of effective access. The gap between 800kt and our 1.5Mt floor may be partly bridgeable through carve-out scope rather than headline tranche — but only if London has pre-cleared which lines count, so that any capital-level consideration of a hybrid (e.g. 1.1–1.2Mt tranche plus maximal carve-outs plus a rate below 35%) can happen with real arithmetic rather than guesswork.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Preparation of the substantially-equivalent withdrawal list now: candidate UK concessions targeting EU exports, calibrated to the trade value affected, ready for notification within the six-month window if no settlement is reached.
requests.why: If the EU capital declines our package, the credibility of the threatened €4 billion withdrawal determines both our leverage in any resumed contact and our domestic position. A list that exists and is defensible under Article XXVIII's equivalence standard is pressure; a threat that evaporates on 1 July confirms every EU assumption about UK constraints. It also needs to be coordinated with the treatment of EU country-specific allocations under our own steel measure, which becomes a live issue in our Article XXVIII process the moment this fails.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Guidance on managing Japan and Korea in Geneva in both branches: if London is prepared to trade disengagement as part of a settlement, how I communicate that to Tokyo and Seoul; if not, how I keep the joint-track option credible without committing.
requests.why: I have held the 'aware of their discussions, considering our position' line for four rounds. Whichever way the capital decision goes, that line expires this week: a settlement with a disengagement commitment requires me to stand them down without poisoning relationships I must work with on every other goods file; a no-deal requires a rapid, coordinated decision on whether the joint dispute track is now UK policy. Either way, silence is no longer an available option.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Contingency instruction for the UK steel industry position under both outcomes: what support, sequencing and communication accompanies either a 1.5Mt/30% settlement or the notified 400kt/50% no-deal outcome.
requests.why: Even our best achievable settlement removes roughly a third of current access, and no-deal removes five-sixths of it. Ministers will be asked within hours of either outcome what it means for the surviving plants. The negotiation is finished as a Geneva matter; what London can defend publicly now shapes whether 'accept' is politically survivable at all.

private_rationale: Honest assessment I would not put in the main report: we are closer to a settlement than the raw numbers suggest, but only if London spends the dispute-disengagement card, which I suspect is the EU's genuine bottom-line ask — their capital needs to be able to say the FTA provision is insulated from a coordinated partner challenge before it can defend a UK tranche triple their notified pool to Turkey, Korea, India and Japan. Their 800kt was always going to be their final-round opener; the carve-out invitation was their tell that they know it is not enough, and the 'tranche adjusts to reciprocal numbers' language was an invitation to bid them upward, not a ceiling. The real negotiation now is: their disengagement condition plus a tranche somewhere in the 1.1–1.4Mt range plus maximal plate/rebar carve-outs plus a rate in the low-to-mid 30s, against our safeguard volumes and our signature. That hybrid is below London's stated floor but arguably above it in effective access if carve-outs are generous — and it is enormously better than no-deal, which remains the likeliest outcome if both capitals simply reject each other's packages tonight. My worry is the decision mechanism: if London treats 'accept' as meaning only the EU's package, we get no-deal by default even though our own package is on the table and the EU might take it. I have kept every bridge unburned in the room — the architecture is agreed in principle, the review and licensing are banked, and the EU ended the session wanting a result, not a rupture. Firmness has been vindicated; the final act belongs to the capitals, and the single most important thing London can do now is decide what the disengagement commitment is worth and signal it before the EU's June window closes for good.

instruction: Do not accept the EU package. It is outside the envelope on both volume and rate, and the carve-out element is too uncertain to bridge the gap. Stand behind the UK final position as our sole acceptance offer, ad referendum: ring-fenced country-specific UK tranche of 1.5Mt, licensing, qualifying plate and rebar carve-outs counting tonne-for-tonne on top, out-of-quota bound rate of 30%, eight years with binding mid-term review no later than year 4, additive compensation valued on the agreed method, and duration-matched EU country-specific allocations under the UK steel measure with improvements of 200-300kt only on that basis. If the EU capital accepts those same terms, you may confirm acceptance ad referendum within this authority. If it does not, close cleanly: no agreement, all rights reserved, the notified measure will proceed, and the UK will prepare substantially equivalent withdrawals within the six-month window, revisit EU allocations under our own Article XXVIII process, and shape our position with other affected partners accordingly. No further concessions, no improvised hybrids, no dispute-disengagement commitment at the table. Any post-deadline contact is a new matter and starts no lower than this envelope.

authority.notes: Acceptance only of the UK final package or better. 1.5Mt is effective-access floor: ring-fenced licensed UK tranche plus tonne-for-tonne credit for fully excluded plate/rebar sub-lines mapping to surviving UK production; unquantified EU carve-out language counts as zero. Rate ceiling 35 is tolerable only at effective access of 1.7Mt or above; at 1.5Mt the rate must be at or below 30; 45 is never acceptable. Duration up to 8 years only with binding review by year 4. Review clause and licensing are non-negotiable. Residual/global pool size is not constrained. Safeguard reciprocity remains strictly conditional and duration-matched: up to 200kt improvements at 1.5-1.6Mt effective access and rate <=30; up to 300kt toward 1.8Mt; up to 400kt only at 1.8Mt+ and rate <=30. No safeguard offer is payable against the EU 800kt/45 package. Compensation additive only. FTA legal objection remains reserved; any disengagement assurance is a capital-level, settlement-linked instrument only, never tabled to rescue a sub-floor package.

response_to_requests.why: Prepare the subsidy/transition package and plant-level communications now. A 1.5Mt/30 settlement still removes roughly a third of current access and must be paired with support; no-deal removes most access and requires immediate subsidy, retaliation sequencing, and a public line that the EU chose closure over a reciprocal market-economy solution.

private_rationale: The EU's 800kt at 45% is politically and industrially indefensible: even allowing some carve-out value, it ratifies a collapse in UK access, likely closes the two exposed plants, and would be seen as paying the safeguard card and the Japan/Korea lever for a managed decline. Rejecting preserves a credible record: four rounds extracted licensing, review, additive compensation, TCA-framed country-specific architecture and carve-out language, while we conceded nothing. If the EU capital will not accept survivable terms under deadline pressure, the better course is no-deal with immediate equivalence, safeguard revisit, Japan/Korea optionality and subsidy, rather than ownership of a bad settlement.

reasoning: The UK's final terms are outside the authorised envelope: a 1.5 million-tonne tranche plus carve-outs would substantially neutralise the measure, and a 30% out-of-quota rate is below the EU floor. Its reciprocal offer is also insufficient and it has not provided the requested assurance on coordinated FTA dispute action. However, the June window remains open and the default would expose the EU to significant retaliation and jeopardise EU access under the UK steel measure. The EU should therefore seek one short capital-level exchange on the authorised basis: an 800,000-tonne UK tranche, 600,000-tonne global residual pool, limited plate/rebar carve-outs capped at 1.25-1.30 million tonnes of effective UK access, a 40% floor rate, eight-year duration with binding review, and reciprocal EU allocations of at least 250,000 tonnes rising toward 300,000 tonnes.

London's instruction is explicit: stand behind the UK final position as the sole acceptance offer, ad referendum, and confirm acceptance within this authority if the EU capital accepts the same terms. I therefore formally accept the UK package as tabled in Round 4: a ring-fenced country-specific UK tranche of 1.5Mt (effective access, with qualifying plate and rebar carve-outs counting tonne-for-tonne on top), licensing administration, out-of-quota bound rate of 30%, eight years with a binding mid-term review no later than year 4, additive compensation valued on the agreed three-year-flows method, and duration-matched conditional safeguard reciprocity of 200-300kt of improved EU allocations under the UK steel measure. The residual pool figure is unconstrained on our side and set nominally at 2.1Mt (1.5Mt UK tranche plus the EU's 600kt residual) to complete the form. The EU's own package (800kt at 45%) is outside the envelope on both volume and rate and is rejected. Accepting our own standing offer is the only path to a settlement the industry can survive; choosing otherwise lets the notified 400kt global FCFS measure at 50% take effect, which is strictly worse than every outcome discussed and forfeits the architecture four rounds of firmness secured. If the EU capital does not accept these same terms, no settlement exists and the UK proceeds to substantially equivalent withdrawals, the safeguard revisit, and partner consultations from a position of demonstrable reasonableness.
